(MarijuanaNews note: A reader informed me this morning that on Friday afternoon the medical cannabis club on La Brea in Hollywood was raided. He went by after 11 P.M. and the police were still there. He talked to three police investigators and asked them what was going on.

He says that this is approximately how the conversation went. I have added a few explanatory notes.)

They said providing marijuana was illegal.

I said what about with a doctors recommendation?

They said you need to be registered with the state agency, which of course is not true.

They said this club were selling to people who were complaining about stress. I said " wasn't stress the biggest killer in America. "
See
 Ricky Williams and Our Paxil Problem. The Media Miss the Point, As Usual.

(MarijuanaNews note: Prop 215 says that doctors can recommend it for anything that they think appropriate.)
See
 Full Text of Proposition 215 Compassionate Use Act of 1996

They said they were supposed to be non profit and they were making a lot of money.
See
 Program notes for the MarijuanaNews World Report for April 21, 2005. Sativex Maker Declares War on Sick and Dying. Students Lead Drugwar Resistance Against Police. 420 A Huge Success In Colorado.

Before that I had asked them how a little old lady was able to get their medicine.

They said the prices compared to the " STREETS " were more expensive (they didn't mention the dangers on the streets, or how an older person is supposed to find a dealer..)

They said they were selling candies and drinks. I said some times I didn't want smoke in my throat and lung and that I liked the candies instead.
See
 No Medicine Is Smoked. Okay, But Why Isn't Cannabis Sold Over-the-Counter? New MAPS/NORML Vaporizer Study Undermines Key Part Of Prohibitionist Party Line On Smoked-Marijuana.

They said I should be upset at the amount of money someone her was making. I thought at how much lawyer cost and the cost of doing business like employees and taxes and backing them up in legal expenses.

(MarijuanaNews note: How about how much the police are making for violating our rights???

I said that this story is exclusive to MarijuanaNews World Report unfortunately because the LA Times has still not reported it. In 2001, they took five days to report the DEA raid on the big Los Angeles Cannabis Resource Center.)

Meanwhile, in Oaksterdam...
(Based on a story in the Contra Costa Times by Guy Ashley)

Alameda County (which is where Oakland is) may be on the verge of going where no local government has gone before: setting up a dispensary for medical cannabis at a county-owned hospital.
See
 Once Upon A Time In the West: The Rise, and Fall, and Rise Again of Oaksterdam. Across the Bay In San Francisco, There Is Trouble In Paradise.

" I would like the county to do this, " said County Supervisor Nate Miley, who will present a proposal today to set up a marijuana dispensary at Fairmont Hospital in San Leandro.
(MarijuanaNews note: Miley is a good guy.)

" It would help bring legitimacy to the whole medical marijuana situation. "

It also may help cool a considerable amount of heat being generated within the ranks over Alameda County's protracted efforts to come up with a law regulating medical marijuana dispensaries.

Much of the heat comes from Sheriff Charles Plummer, who says he is so frustrated by the lack of resolution that he has set a June 17 deadline for the county to finalize a marijuana dispensary ordinance.

If the county misses the deadline, Plummer says he will cite federal law and order his deputies to shut down the seven dispensaries now doing business in unincorporated Alameda County.
(MarijuanaNews note: But please note: NOT Oaksterdam.)

" If they don't come up with an ordinance, they will see this is the real deal, " he said.

(MarijuanaNews note: However, the Contra Costa paper did explain that if he does so, he will violating the state Constitution:

On April 6, 2005 California AG Lockyer stated that, both generally and in the specific context of interpreting the Compassionate Use Act -- it is not the province of state courts to enforce federal laws. And this is precisely what the California state Constitution says.)
 See
 California Constitution Specifically Prohibits State Officials From Using Federal Laws As An Excuse For Not Enforcing State Laws Like Prop 215 Without A Court Ruling. Great Orange County Register Editorial.

A spokeswoman for the federal Drug Enforcement Administration, Casey McEnry, said she would not speculate on whether federal authorities would try to stop a marijuana dispensary on county property.

" Selling marijuana is still in violation of federal law no matter where it's sold, " she said. " No agency is above the law. "

(MarijuanaNews note: Except for the Drug Czar's office which regularly violates various laws about Feds lobbying for state laws.)

Albert McKeon reported in the Nashua Telegraph that the New Hampshire state Senate last week rejected a House proposal that would have opened the door to a strictly regulated hemp industry.

We live in a world of total misinformation, said Greg McCrone, a pharmacist at Herbal Path in Dover, a store that sells hemp products. Whatever regime is in power twists facts time to time.

Some hemp supporters claim that state law enforcement persuaded gullible Senate members that the growth of hemp would encourage a twin marijuana industry. But Sen. Margaret Hassan, D-Exeter, said she and her colleagues did their homework on the bill.

She and other senators could not support the bill, not just because of current law enforcement opposition but also the fact that the federal government labels it a controlled substance. Another State versus feds issue

Police officers testified they cannot differentiate marijuana and hemp, but farmers claim each plant is relatively easy to distinguish.

and

It's intentional ignorance, said Mark Lathrop of Chesterfield, chairman of the N.H. Hemp Council. It's not law enforcement's job to create policy but to enforce policy made for them.

(MarijuanaNews note: But a high school education and a badge make you an experts on everything! Pharmacology, sociology, and in Canada even on US trade policy)

Meanwhile in Alaska, just two days after Gov. Frank Murkowski declared it one of his " must have " bills, his recrim bill appears dead for this legislative session. He was attempting to overturn the Alaska Supreme Court ruling in September that said adults have the right to possess less than four ounces for personal use in their own homes. The court ruled it is protected under the strong right to privacy in the state constitution.
See
 Program Notes for the MarijuanaNews World Report for April 28, 2005 Dutch Mayors And People Favor Legalization. Czar's Helper Lies To Jamaicans. Alaska Governor Dumps Public Defender. ACLU Sues DEA.
and
 Lies and Hatred From Former US Attorney In Alaska. As Bad As It Gets.

The bill would also make possession of over four ounces of cannabis a felony.

With the Legislature scheduled to adjourn for the year on Tuesday, lawmakers said Saturday the bill is out of time.

If the governor forces the Legislature into a special session, Murkowski could try to revive it. Even if it passed, wouldn't be enough to trump the court ruling.

But the bill contains a series of " findings " asserting the harms of marijuana. The governor's strategy is to use those findings in court, along with the legislative record that comes with passing the bill.

The idea is that it would convince the courts that the state has an overriding interest in making all marijuana illegal, despite the right to privacy.

She said she thinks the bill didn't move quickly enough because it came with a 3-foot stack of background material for legislators to digest before approving all the findings about pot's harms.

Anchorage Republican Rep. Kevin Meyer, co-chair of the House Finance Committee, said " It's not a real top priority of anybody except the governor.

On a much sadder note:
See
America Sentenced to Life In Prison For Marijuana. Really! Another One We Couldn't Make Up. And As Usual, It Is Even Worse for Others. DEAland's War On Cannabis Disastrous for Poor Countries.

Singapore has rejected last-ditch appeals to spare a father convicted of smuggling a kilo of cannabis from neighboring Malaysia who is going to hang Friday.

Shanmugam Murugesu, 38, received a mandatory death sentence last year after he was caught returning by motorcycle from neighboring Malaysia in August 2003.

Murugesu is a former jet ski champion, military veteran and civil servant, with no criminal record. He was arrested in August 2003 after six packets containing a total of just over a kilo of cannabis were found in his bags when he returned home after a trip to Malaysia which also has the death penalty for cannabis.

Under Singaporean law, anyone possessing more than 500 grams (17.64 ounces) of marijuana is presumed to be trafficking and faces death if found guilty.

Opposition and civic groups had launched a last-minute campaign to save Murugesu. His twin 14-year-old sons, who will become orphaned if Murugesu dies, have been handing out fliers, asking Singaporeans to help save their father.

Murugesu:The financial burdens on me were heavy as I had to look after the my sons, my nieces, nephews and my mother ... who is in her seventies, is in poor health, unable to work.

Last week, London-based rights group Amnesty International launched an urgent appeal on his behalf. Amnesty International claims Singapore has the world's highest per capita rate of executions.

In its 2004 annual report, the group said executions in Singapore are " shrouded in secrecy. " Singapore rejected the report, saying it was full of " misrepresentations and distortions. "

Of 138 people hanged in Singapore in the five years ending January 2004, 110 were convicted of drug offenses, according to the country's Central Narcotics Bureau.

Only Six death row inmates have been granted clemency since Singapore's independence from Malaysia in 1965, the Straits Times newspaper said Monday .

Why would anyone visit these barbarous countries??

It is interesting to note that Murugesu admitted to knowing about one of the packets, containing 300g, but nothing about the others.

That may seem dubious, but a story from Australia raises an interesting point.

Australian Federal Opposition spokesman for foreign affairs Kevin Rudd is seeking more details from Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer on reports that an Australian man found marijuana in his luggage upon arrival in Indonesia, and was told to flush it down the toilet by Australian consulate officials.

The Department of Foreign Affairs and the Vice Consul in Bali have confirmed they received a call from a Melbourne man saying he found drugs in his bag after flying in from Melbourne in 1997.

But the authorities say the form of disposal was only one of several options canvassed.

Frankly, I think that it was excellent advice. What should he have done? Call the local thuggery?

Rudd says it is a serious development and may impact on the Schapelle Corby case. Corby is facing a possible death penalty in Indonesia because cannabis was found in her suitcase and she claims that she did not know that it was there.
